abstract: This study analyzes how generative AI tools like ChatGPT are reshaping freelance labor markets. Using data from a major international freelancing platform covering nearly 1.73 million job posts from July 2021 to July 2023, researchers found that freelancers in AI-vulnerable professions experienced a 21% fall in weekly demand for their skills within seven months of ChatGPT's launch. While writing jobs fell 30% and coding fell 20%, paradoxically wages rose slightly for automation-prone roles, suggesting employers still demand human expertise for complex tasks while simpler jobs are being replaced by AI.
keyFindings: Online freelancers in professions vulnerable to automation saw a 21% fall in weekly demand for their skills seven months after ChatGPT's launch compared to those with manual-focused jobs.
Writing jobs experienced a 30% decline in demand, while coding jobs fell 20%, indicating differential impacts across automation-prone professions.
Wages for automation-prone jobs rose slightly despite declining demand, suggesting employers still value human expertise for complex tasks while AI replaces simpler, shorter-term work.
Visual creative professions like graphic design and 3D rendering experienced a 13% fall in demand following the advent of text-to-image generation AI.
The analysis covered nearly 1.73 million unique job posts from a major international freelancing platform over a two-year period spanning July 2021 to July 2023.
methodology: Analysis of nearly 1.73 million unique job posts from a major international freelancing platform covering the period July 2021 to July 2023. Researchers examined changes in job volume and type following ChatGPT's launch in November 2022. Supplementary validation included pattern analysis from Google search trends related to generative AI awareness and examination of work exposure metrics to artificial intelligence. The study expanded beyond previous research focused on writing to include coding, engineering, software development, web/app development, graphic design, and other professions. Comparisons were made between jobs more vulnerable to automation versus those involving manual tasks.
qualifiers: The study focuses on online freelance markets, which are short-term, tightly defined, and transactional in nature—findings may not directly apply to traditional corporate environments. Authors note that while job demand fell, there is no direct means to measure job complexity, though estimates were derived from job descriptions. The analysis covers a two-year period through July 2023, providing a limited timeframe since ChatGPT's launch in November 2022. The authors acknowledge that factors such as freelancer quality and skills could affect the supply-side impact. They raise open questions about whether findings are more pronounced in freelance markets than traditional employment and whether overall job postings are falling globally.
